stage: HISTORIE (engine stage 6) - fractal axis + competing frames - cache
disputedNote: Even where this story begins is disputed - picking a start date is itself a position. Frames change emphasis and annotation, never the record.

frames.label: June 2026 strikes
frames.note: Story begins when Pakistani airstrikes hit Kunar and other eastern districts after a month of relative calm following the Eid pause, killing civilians the Taliban administration counts as 13 including 11 children. Under this frame the situation reads as a sudden rupture of a fragile ceasefire and a new round of cross-border fire. This is the frame most wire reports and Indian outlets like DD News and News On AIR open with.

frames.label: Aug 2021 Taliban return
frames.note: Story begins when the Taliban retook Kabul and TTP attacks on Pakistani soil escalated, with Islamabad arguing militants now operate freely from Afghan territory. Under this frame the strikes read as counterterrorism against a neighbor harboring armed groups, and Afghan retaliation reads as state sponsorship surfacing. This is the frame Pakistani security commentary in Daily Times and Press TV opens with.

bands.label: Renewed strikes after Eid pause
bands.summary: An Eid-ul-Fitr pause collapses as Pakistani airstrikes hit eastern Afghanistan, the Taliban claims 13 civilians killed including children, and Afghan forces stage retaliatory attacks along the Durand Line.

nodes.title: Eid pause halts cross-border fire
nodes.what: Pakistan and Afghanistan announce a temporary pause in fighting along the Durand Line in view of Eid, opening roughly a month of relative calm after earlier exchanges. The arrangement is announced bilaterally and not formalized as a written ceasefire. Both governments use the lull to reposition forces and shift to diplomatic messaging.

nodes.title: Pakistani airstrikes hit Kunar, ending the calm
nodes.what: Pakistani aircraft strike targets in Kunar and adjoining eastern districts of Afghanistan, breaking the post-Eid lull. Initial reports describe at least seven dead and several wounded. Islamabad describes the operation as targeting militant infrastructure across the frontier.

nodes.title: Taliban administration says 13 civilians killed, including 11 children
nodes.what: The Taliban administration in Kabul says the Pakistani strikes killed at least 13 civilians in eastern Afghanistan, with 11 of the dead identified as children. Spokesmen describe the targets as residential areas and call the operation a violation of Afghan sovereignty.
nodes.disputed: Pakistani security commentary describes the targets as TTP fighters and infrastructure across the border; the Taliban administration describes the same sites as homes and the dead as civilians, including 11 children.

nodes.title: Afghan forces stage retaliatory attacks along the Durand Line
nodes.what: Afghan authorities announce retaliatory operations at multiple points along the Durand Line in response to the strikes. Kabul says Taliban forces killed 30 Pakistani soldiers in the resulting clashes. Pakistani officials acknowledge the firefights but contest the casualty figures.
nodes.disputed: News On AIR and Afghan officials describe the cross-border action as a calibrated retaliation that inflicted heavy Pakistani military losses; Pakistani security commentary describes the same exchanges as routine border defense against Taliban-enabled attacks.

nodes.title: Pakistani rhetoric escalates; coverage frames an 'open war'
nodes.what: Indian and regional outlets report Pakistani statements escalating to an 'open war' posture toward Kabul after the strikes and retaliation. Analyses cite a strategy of pressuring the Taliban administration through repeated cross-border operations. Commentary disputes whether Islamabad's existing regional pacts deter further escalation.

nodes.title: Sharif defends Durand Line fencing as a security necessity
nodes.what: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif publicly defends the fencing of the Durand Line as essential for Pakistan's security, responding to renewed Afghan objections during the post-strike standoff. The Taliban administration rejects both the fence and the boundary itself as colonial impositions. The exchange reframes the latest fighting as part of a longer border dispute.
nodes.disputed: Sharif describes the fence as a defensive measure against militant infiltration; Kabul and Afghan commentators describe it as unilateral consolidation of a boundary they have never formally accepted.

bands.label: Post-Taliban return tensions
bands.summary: After the Taliban retake Kabul, TTP attacks inside Pakistan rise sharply, Islamabad conducts repeated cross-border strikes, and Afghan-Pakistani relations cycle through clashes, fence disputes, and short ceasefires.

nodes.title: Taliban retake Kabul as US withdrawal completes
nodes.what: The Taliban entered Kabul as President Ashraf Ghani fled and the Western-backed government collapsed. The takeover ended two decades of US-led presence and brought to power a movement Pakistan had long been accused of supporting, while also emboldening the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan operating along the border.

nodes.title: Pakistani airstrikes hit Khost and Kunar provinces
nodes.what: Pakistani aircraft struck targets inside Afghanistan's Khost and Kunar provinces, with Afghan officials reporting dozens of civilians killed including women and children. Islamabad said the operation targeted TTP militants responsible for attacks in North Waziristan, while the Taliban administration summoned Pakistan's ambassador in protest.
nodes.disputed: Pakistani officials described the strikes as counterterrorism against TTP camps; the Taliban Foreign Ministry described them as violations of Afghan sovereignty that killed civilians.

nodes.title: TTP ends ceasefire with Pakistan
nodes.what: The Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan formally ended a months-long ceasefire with the Pakistani state and ordered its fighters to resume attacks nationwide. The breakdown triggered a sharp rise in militant violence in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan and hardened Islamabad's posture toward the Afghan Taliban administration.

nodes.title: Pakistan orders mass expulsion of undocumented Afghans
nodes.what: Pakistan's caretaker government announced that all undocumented foreigners, mainly Afghans, would have to leave by 1 November or face deportation. Hundreds of thousands crossed back into Afghanistan in the following weeks, straining Taliban-administered border posts and deepening diplomatic friction.

nodes.title: Pakistan conducts air operation inside Afghanistan
nodes.what: Pakistani jets struck what Islamabad called TTP hideouts in Khost and Paktika provinces, days after a militant attack killed seven Pakistani soldiers in North Waziristan. Taliban authorities reported civilian deaths and announced retaliatory fire across the border in Kurram and North Waziristan.
nodes.disputed: Pakistan's Foreign Office described the action as intelligence-based anti-terror strikes; Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid described it as an attack on civilian homes that killed women and children.

nodes.title: Strikes on Paktika trigger border clashes
nodes.what: Pakistani airstrikes in Paktika's Barmal district killed dozens, with the Taliban saying many of the dead were refugees from Waziristan. Afghan forces responded with cross-border fire and ground actions at several points along the Durand Line in the following days.

nodes.title: Eid-ul-Fitr pause quiets the frontier
nodes.what: Around Eid-ul-Fitr, cross-border firing and air operations subsided into a relative lull that held through April and into May. Officials on both sides publicly described the calm as fragile, and TTP attacks inside Pakistan continued at a lower tempo before the pause broke down in June.
